claims.statement: Dependencies guide declares FPT/GHEC and Free/Pro/Team/Enterprise Cloud plans, with repository triage minimum; GHES coverage is not declared here. Missing authority or feature availability remains unknown, not passing.

Blocked-by means this issue depends on another; blocking means this issue prevents another. UI selects related issues and removal deselects exact relationships. A blocked icon is display evidence, not enforced prohibition on closure or merging.

CLI examples document creation blocked-by/blocking lists, add/remove relationship flags, and blockedBy/blocking JSON fields. Installed CLI version, target repository identity and write permissions require verification; examples are not executed.
The guide does not define transitive blocking, cycle rejection, relationship limits, atomic multi-write behavior or rollback. These remain unspecified rather than assumed enforced.

Sub-issue guide declares FPT/GHEC/GHES wildcard and triage minimum. Pinned projects variable resolves to 100 sub-issues per parent and guide limits nesting to eight levels; these are platform constraints, not adopted workload thresholds.

Creation creates a new child with optional type, assignees, labels, project and milestone metadata. Existing children can be selected across repositories; access and exact repository issue identity must be checked rather than assuming parent permissions transfer.
Hierarchy is distinct from blocking dependencies: parent and progress fields support Projects views/grouping/filtering but are not proof prerequisite enforcement or accepted completion.

CLI examples distinguish creating with parent, adding existing comma-separated issue references, removing a child from a parent and removing parent from the child. Relationship removal is not issue deletion; runtime compatibility and recovery are unverified.
Tasklist-era redirects point to this sub-issue guide; alias routing does not establish historical tasklist behavior parity or migrated state assurance.

Browsing guide and shared fragment describe expandable multilevel hierarchy, parent-header navigation and Project hierarchy fields. Navigation claims do not establish complete inaccessible-descendant visibility.

CLI view shows parent reference, child state and progress; JSON requests parent/subIssues/subIssuesSummary. Example one of three closed gives 33 percent but is not a normative recursive denominator or independently verified acceptance metric.

Hierarchy display, closed lifecycle state and progress percentages must remain separate from policy acceptance, current verification evidence and native enforcement; no new authority is granted by viewing relationships.
